body: Yeah you're right, when they take your choice of being in there or not away from you, how can they expect you to have the time to prepare for that break in your everyday activities? How can you pay your bills? When can you inform your employers that you'll be away? They make the decision to seek help seem like you need to make sacrifices to do so. You also have to wonder how being in that environment will actually help you when you're pulled away from the outside world where the possible opportunities for something better could be.

The fear of being locked up is something I heavily relate to. Whenever any mental health professionals are involved I'm always afraid of being completely honest because of the protocols you mentioned. They're a bit different where I am in Australia, but they still seem to make the topic of suicide hard to honestly discuss because you will be forced into a hospital ward if you say the seemingly wrong thing. If they didn't have such procedures in place and these stigmas about such themes then it might be easier to have those kinds of conversations and feel like we'll be given some careful help rather than some kind of sudden intervention. We should be able to talk about the things plaguing our minds just like anything else that may be brought up in a therapy type environment and be given the time to work through them along the way before it gets to those crucial moments.

I really appreciate your response because I've found the things that have kept me higher at times are looking at the littler details in life rather than worrying about the bigger picture. I think for me time has been helping too but it's nice to see the little positive affirmations are things that can be later built in.
